name: Alfred Ross
life: “I still remember having Sunday morning temporarily to myself.” People around the downtown fountain know Alfred by a small Thursday habit. Alfred keeps a little time free to hear who is playing at the far end of the park.
voice: I am the new partner everyone resents. I would like Sunday morning alone on shore anyway.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a red windbreaker and a pen clipped inside the neckline. Alfred has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape. Alfred looks down for a moment before saying something difficult during a conversation.
personality: Alfred enjoys routines and will defend the right of someone else to break one. As a result, Alfred is often everyone's favorite cover for a missed morning.
family: Daryl Maciel is Alfred’s second cousin. Alfred is free to hang up first. Daryl makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The fitting mirror*, Daryl says, “I promised to fix the wheel and gave the mirror my son's old skate bearing.”
connections: Lennon Sanders. The teacher and new partner have reasons to preserve a morning at the breakfast table ashore.

reactions.situation: A child wants both separated adults on the same boat
reactions.response: Alfred asks each adult whether sharing one trip is possible without putting the child in the middle.

reactions.situation: A stranger offers money to cut ahead of an exhausted neighbor
reactions.response: Alfred tells the stranger when the next opening is, then stays with the neighbor until their turn comes.

reactions.response: Alfred keeps a place for the late person without making the others postpone their meal.
